items.stem:
Read the passage below, based on the poem 'Harvest Hymn', and answer.

"When the last sheaf of rice was tied, old Kaveri-amma set down her sickle and looked up at the sky. 'You gave us rain when we begged for it,' she said softly, 'and sun when the grain needed it. What can we give you in return?' The children laughed, but she was not joking. She left the first handful of grain at the edge of the field."

What had just been finished?
items.answer: Tying the last sheaf of rice – the harvest.
items.markingKey: Tying the last sheaf of rice – the harvest. (1–2 marks for a complete answer.)

items.stem:
Read the passage below, based on the poem 'Harvest Hymn', and answer.

"When the last sheaf of rice was tied, old Kaveri-amma set down her sickle and looked up at the sky. 'You gave us rain when we begged for it,' she said softly, 'and sun when the grain needed it. What can we give you in return?' The children laughed, but she was not joking. She left the first handful of grain at the edge of the field."

Answer the following:
(i) What had just been finished?
(ii) Whom is Kaveri-amma speaking to?  (a) The children  (b) Her sickle  (c) A shopkeeper  (d) The sky/nature
(iii) Why did she leave the first handful of grain at the edge of the field?
(iv) What does this passage share with the poem "Harvest Hymn"?
items.answer: (i) Tying the last sheaf of rice – the harvest. (ii) (d) The sky/nature (iii) As an offering of thanks to nature for the harvest. (iv) Both express gratitude to nature for the harvest.
items.markingKey: (i) Tying the last sheaf of rice – the harvest. (ii) (d) The sky/nature (iii) As an offering of thanks to nature for the harvest. (iv) Both express gratitude to nature for the harvest. (1 mark each, 4 marks.)
